entry.label: Boundary
entry.description: A boundary makes inquiry and action possible by limiting what must be handled at once. It also externalises people, effects and responsibilities. Good systems work therefore treats boundary choice as practical, political and ethical.
entry.canonical_definition: A purpose- and observer-dependent distinction that marks what is treated as inside, outside or marginal to a system of concern and thereby shapes explanation, legitimacy and intervention.

profile.title: Boundary
profile.canonical_definition: A purpose- and observer-dependent distinction that marks what is treated as inside, outside or marginal to a system of concern and thereby shapes explanation, legitimacy and intervention.
profile.summary: A boundary makes inquiry and action possible by limiting what must be handled at once. It also externalises people, effects and responsibilities. Good systems work therefore treats boundary choice as practical, political and ethical.
profile.why_it_matters: Boundaries decide who counts, what becomes a cost, which outcomes are visible and where responsibility stops. Changing the boundary can change the apparent problem without changing any events.
practice_connections: state the current boundary and purpose
ask who and what is excluded
strengthen, suspend, cross, reframe or change boundaries deliberately
common_misreadings: open systems have no meaningful boundaries
